[[File:Skein Mix Function.png|thumb|200px|Threefish Mix Function]]
'''Skein''' is a [[cryptographic hash function]] and one of five finalists in the [[NIST hash function competition]]. Entered as a candidate to become the [[SHA-3]] standard, the successor of [[SHA-1]] and [[SHA-2]], it ultimately lost to NIST hash candidate [[Keccak]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.nist.gov/itl/csd/sha-100212.cfm |title=NIST Selects Winner of Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-3) Competition |date=2012-10-02|journal=[[NIST]] |accessdate=2012-10-02}}</ref>

The name Skein refers to how the Skein function intertwines the input, similar to a [[wikt:skein|skein]] of yarn.<ref name=skein>{{cite web |date=2010-10-01 |author=Ferguson |title=The Skein Hash Function Family |url=http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein1.3.pdf |display-authors=etal |access-date=2010-12-15 |archive-date=2014-08-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140824053109/http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein1.3.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Skein was designed to natively support arbitrary, variable-length outputs, so it can be considered an [[extendable-output function]] (XOF).{{cn|date=May 2026}}

== History ==
Skein was created by [[Bruce Schneier]], [[Niels Ferguson]], [[Stefan Lucks]], Doug Whiting, [[Mihir Bellare]], Tadayoshi Kohno, [[Jon Callas]] and Jesse Walker.

Skein is based on the [[Threefish]] [[tweakable block cipher|tweakable]] [[block cipher]] compressed using [[Unique Block Iteration]] (UBI) chaining mode, a variant of the [[Matyas–Meyer–Oseas]] hash mode,<ref>http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein1.3.pdf {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140824053109/http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein1.3.pdf |date=2014-08-24 }} p. 6</ref> while leveraging an optional low-overhead argument-system for flexibility.

Skein's algorithm and a [[reference implementation]] was given to [[public domain]].<ref>[http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein_NIST_CD_121508.zip skein_NIST_CD_121508.zip] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610070200/http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein_NIST_CD_121508.zip |date=2016-06-10 }} on skein-hash.info, skein.c ''"Implementation of the Skein hash function. Source code author: Doug Whiting, 2008. This algorithm and source code is released to the public domain."''</ref>

== Functionality ==
Skein supports internal state sizes of 256, 512 and 1024 bits, and arbitrary output sizes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://it.slashdot.org/article.pl?sid=08/10/31/1426215|title=Now From Bruce Schneier, the Skein Hash Function |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=[[Slashdot]] |accessdate=2008-10-31}}</ref>

The authors claim 6.1 [[cycles per byte]] for any output size on an [[Intel Core 2]] Duo in 64-bit mode.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein1.3.pdf |title=Paper describing the hash function, Version 1.3 (2010-10-01) |access-date=2010-12-15 |archive-date=2014-08-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140824053109/http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/skein1.3.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The core of Threefish is based on a MIX function that transforms 2 64-bit words using a single addition, rotation by a constant and XOR. The UBI chaining mode combines an input chaining value with an arbitrary length input string and produces a fixed size output.

Threefish's [[nonlinearity]] comes entirely from the combination of addition operations and [[Exclusive or|exclusive-OR]]s; it does not use [[S-box]]es.  The function is optimized for 64-bit processors, and the Skein paper defines optional features such as randomized [[Hash function|hashing]], [[parallelizable]] [[Merkle tree|tree hashing]], a [[stream cipher]], personalization, and a [[key derivation function]].

==Cryptanalysis==
In October 2010, an attack that combines [[rotational cryptanalysis]] with the [[rebound attack]] was published. The attack finds rotational collisions for 53 of 72 rounds in Threefish-256, and 57 of 72 rounds in Threefish-512. It also affects the Skein hash function.<ref name=rotational-rebound>{{cite journal |author1=Dmitry Khovratovich |author2=Ivica Nikolic |author3=Christian Rechberger |date=2010-10-20 |title=Rotational Rebound Attacks on Reduced Skein |journal=Cryptology ePrint Archive |url=http://eprint.iacr.org/2010/538 }}</ref> This is a follow-up to the earlier attack published in February, which breaks 39 and 42 rounds respectively.<ref>{{cite web |year=2010 |author1=Dmitry Khovratovich |author2=Ivica Nikolić |name-list-style=amp |title=Rotational Cryptanalysis of ARX |publisher=[[University of Luxembourg]] |url=http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/axr.pdf |access-date=2010-10-25 |archive-date=2013-01-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130126083241/http://www.skein-hash.info/sites/default/files/axr.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The Skein team tweaked the [[key schedule]] constant for round 3 of the NIST hash function competition, to make this attack less effective, even though they believe the hash would still be secure without these tweaks.<ref name=skein />

==Examples of Skein hashes==
Hash values of empty string.
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-256-256("")</span>
 c8877087da56e072870daa843f176e9453115929094c3a40c463a196c29bf7ba
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-512-256("")</span>
 39ccc4554a8b31853b9de7a1fe638a24cce6b35a55f2431009e18780335d2621
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-512-512("")</span>
 bc5b4c50925519c290cc634277ae3d6257212395cba733bbad37a4af0fa06af41fca7903d06564fea7a2d3730dbdb80c1f85562dfcc070334ea4d1d9e72cba7a

Even a small change in the message will (with overwhelming probability) result in a mostly different hash, due to the [[avalanche effect]]. For example, adding a period to the end of the sentence:
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-512-256("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]]")</span>
 b3250457e05d3060b1a4bbc1428bc75a3f525ca389aeab96cfa34638d96e492a
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-512-256("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]].")</span>
 41e829d7fca71c7d7154ed8fc8a069f274dd664ae0ed29d365d919f4e575eebb
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-512-512("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]]")</span>
 94c2ae036dba8783d0b3f7d6cc111ff810702f5c77707999be7e1c9486ff238a7044de734293147359b4ac7e1d09cd247c351d69826b78dcddd951f0ef912713
 <span style="color: green;">Skein-512-512("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]].")</span>
 658223cb3d69b5e76e3588ca63feffba0dc2ead38a95d0650564f2a39da8e83fbb42c9d6ad9e03fbfde8a25a880357d457dbd6f74cbcb5e728979577dbce5436

===Implementations===
* [http://www.skein-hash.info/SPARKSkein-release SPARKSkein] – an implementation of Skein in [[SPARK (programming language)|SPARK]], with proofs of type-safety
* [[Botan (programming library)|Botan]] contains a C++ implementation of Skein-512
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20090913132131/http://www.sriramkrishnan.com/blog/2009/08/nskein-skein-implementation-net.html nskein] – a .NET implementation of Skein with support for all block sizes
* [http://packages.python.org/pyskein/ pyskein] Skein module for Python
* [https://github.com/jedisct1/PHP-Skein-Hash PHP-Skein-Hash] Skein hash for PHP on GitHub
* [https://metacpan.org/module/Digest::Skein Digest::Skein], an implementation in C and Perl
* [http://code.google.com/p/skeinfish/ skeinfish] A C# implementation of Skein and Threefish (based on version 1.3)
* [http://www.h2database.com/skein/index.html Java, Scala, and Javascript implementations of Skein 512-512 (based on version 1.3)]
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081214181836/http://www.xs4all.nl/~warper/ A Java implementation of Skein (based on version 1.1)]
* [http://www.skein-hash.info/node/30 An implementation of Skein in Ada]
* [https://github.com/basho/skerl skerl], Skein hash function for Erlang, via NIFs
* [https://sourceforge.net/p/skeinbash/home/Home/ Skein 512-512 implemented in Bash]
* [http://hackage.haskell.org/package/cryptohash Skein implemented in Haskell]
* [http://cryptography.gmu.edu/athena/index.php?id=source_codes VHDL source code] developed by the Cryptographic Engineering Research Group (CERG) at [[George Mason University]]
* [http://www.coderslagoon.com/#skeinr skeinr] Skein implemented in Ruby
* [http://www.syntax-k.de/projekte/fhreefish/ fhreefish] An efficient implementation of Skein-256 for 8-bit Atmel AVR microcontrollers, meeting the performance estimates outlined in the official specification
